name: Jesus
note: From Nazareth in Galilee. Mark opens by calling him Christ, the Son of God, and spends the rest of the book on what that means.

name: John the Baptist
note: A prophet in the wilderness who calls people to repent and baptizes them in the Jordan.

name: Simon Peter
note: A fisherman from Capernaum, the first disciple called and the most prominent of the twelve.

name: Andrew
note: Peter's brother, also a fisherman.

name: James
note: Son of Zebedee, called with his brother John from their father's boat.

name: John
note: Son of Zebedee and brother of James.

name: A man in the synagogue
note: Unnamed in Mark; the first person Jesus frees from an unclean spirit.

name: Peter's mother-in-law
note: Lived in Peter's house in Capernaum.

name: A man with a skin disease
note: Cut off from the community by the purity laws until a priest declared him clean.

name: A paralyzed man
note: Brought to Jesus on a mat by his friends.

name: The four friends
note: The men who carried the paralyzed man and dug through the roof.

name: Scribes and Pharisees
note: Scribes were experts in the law, and Pharisees taught careful keeping of it. They are Jesus' main opponents in Galilee.

name: Levi
note: A tax collector, the son of Alphaeus, who becomes a follower of Jesus; traditionally the same man as Matthew.

name: David
note: Israel's great king, from whose line the Christ was expected.

name: The disciples
note: Jesus' followers, starting with the four fishermen. Later, the twelve.

name: A man with a withered hand
note: Healed in a synagogue on the Sabbath.

name: The Herodians
note: Supporters of the Herod family and its Rome-backed rule.

name: The crowds
note: Ordinary people from Galilee, Judea, and beyond who follow Jesus to listen and be healed.

name: The twelve
note: Peter, Andrew, James, John, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas Iscariot.

name: Judas Iscariot
note: One of the twelve, who later betrays Jesus.

name: Jesus' mother and brothers
note: His family in Nazareth. His brothers are named in 6:3.

name: The man from the tombs
note: Violent and isolated, he becomes the first Gentile missionary in Mark.

name: Jairus
note: A leader of the synagogue, in Galilee.

name: Jairus' daughter
note: A girl of twelve.

name: The woman with the flow of blood
note: Unnamed; ill and, by the purity laws, cut off for twelve years.

name: Herod Antipas
note: Son of Herod the Great; ruled Galilee and Perea as tetrarch.

name: Herodias
note: Antipas' wife, formerly married to his brother.

name: Herodias' daughter
note: Unnamed in Mark; Josephus calls her Salome.

name: The Syrophoenician woman
note: A Greek woman from the region of Tyre.

name: The deaf man
note: Brought by friends in the Decapolis.

name: The blind man of Bethsaida
note: Healed in two stages.
